name: Dow

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Dow Chemical Company logo.svg; Dow Inc. redirects to that article)

description: Dow is a maker of plastics and chemicals: polyethylene and other plastics for packaging (Packaging & Specialty Plastics, 50% of FY2025 sales), polyurethane and industrial intermediates (Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure, 28%), and silicones, coatings ingredients and consumer materials (Performance Materials & Coatings, 20%). It buys ethane, propane, naphtha and natural gas, turns them into ethylene and propylene at its own crackers, and sells derivatives to packaging, construction, auto and consumer makers; prices follow the industry cycle, not brand pricing. FY2025 was a loss year: net sales fell to $39,968M, segment operating EBIT to $422M in total, and a net loss of $2,623M included $1,856M of restructuring, goodwill and asset charges and a halved dividend. Then Q2 2026 net sales jumped to $12,092M from $10,104M and Packaging & Specialty Plastics EBIT to $1,278M from $71M; the sources read do not explain the jump.

gics.note: Conventional filing: sector and sub-industry from Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30); industry group and industry not on that page, so null. EDGAR SIC 2821 (Plastic Materials, Synthetic Resins).

hq.note: EDGAR business address and Wikipedia S&P 500 list both Midland, MI. The FY2025 10-K is a combined filing of Dow Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiary The Dow Chemical Company (TDCC).

employees.note: Approximately 34,600 permanent full-time employees (FY2025 10-K). In January 2026 the Board approved 'Transform to Outperform', including a workforce reduction of about 4,500 roles by end of 2027 (Q2 2026 10-Q).

businessLines.name: Packaging & Specialty Plastics
businessLines.how: Bulk resin sales to converters and packagers priced off feedstock costs and industry supply and demand (profit is the gap between feedstock cost and selling price); the Hydrocarbons & Energy business is mostly internal, supplying Dow's own derivative plants.
businessLines.description: Hydrocarbons & Energy (buys feedstocks, makes ethylene, propylene, benzene and butadiene, energy used inside Dow) plus Packaging and Specialty Plastics (polyethylene and specialty plastics such as polyolefin elastomers for food packaging, health and hygiene, wire and cable, footwear, photovoltaic encapsulants and adhesives). Includes shares of joint ventures EQUATE and TKOC (Kuwait, 42.5%), Map Ta Phut (Thailand), Sadara (Saudi Arabia, 35%), and SCGC-Dow (50%).

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $2,373M on $21,776M. Share not shown because the Industrial Intermediates segment was negative; the three segments and corporate sum to $422M. Q2 2026 Operating EBIT $1,278M on $6,385M sales vs $71M on $5,025M; H1 2026 sales $11,304M.

businessLines.name: Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure
businessLines.how: Chemical makers and manufacturers buy intermediates by contract or spot and pay for polyurethane foam systems and construction chemicals; profit is the spread between feedstock/energy cost and selling prices, plus equity income from Sadara and other joint ventures.
businessLines.description: Industrial Solutions (ingredients for consumer health, agriculture, aircraft deicing fluids, solvents, heat-transfer fluids, lubricants) and Polyurethanes & Construction Chemicals (world's largest producer of propylene oxide, propylene glycol and polyether polyols, aromatic isocyanates, chlor-alkali and vinyl, construction chemicals).

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $125M on $11,869M. A $690M goodwill impairment on the Polyurethanes & Construction Chemicals reporting unit and a $303M Latin America chlor-alkali/propylene oxide impairment were recorded in 2025 (of which the $303M includes $71M in Packaging & Specialty Plastics). Q2 2026 EBIT $246M on $3,166M vs -$185M.

businessLines.marketShare: Polyurethanes business is the world's largest producer of propylene oxide, propylene glycol and polyether polyols (per the 10-K); no percentage given.

businessLines.name: Performance Materials & Coatings
businessLines.how: Paint makers and consumer-goods and electronics manufacturers buy ingredients and silicones under supply contracts; revenue follows industrial and construction activity and specialty pricing.
businessLines.description: Coatings & Performance Monomers (coating materials such as acrylic binders for architectural and industrial paints, and performance monomers) and Consumer Solutions (silicones for consumer and electronics, home and personal care, infrastructure, mobility).

businessLines.name: Corporate
businessLines.how: Not a business line; corporate costs and small other sales.
businessLines.description: Corporate and other items, including sales not in the three segments.

whatsNext.text: Fort Saskatchewan (Alberta) Path2Zero net-zero ethylene complex delayed by two years: first and second phases now expected to start up by end of 2029 and 2030
Shut down an ethylene cracker in Bohlen, Germany by end of 2027
'Transform to Outperform' cost programme (about 4,500 roles) substantially complete by end of 2027; pretax severance charges $27M in Q1 and $445M in Q2 2026
Xycle advanced-recycling plant (Rotterdam) expected fully operational by end of 2026
